newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers vote to keep council president.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers vote to keep council president.

text.p: Hong Kong legislators on Wednesday voted against a motion aimed at removing the legislature's president, also a member of an interim chamber set up to replace the elected body in July, media said.
Andrew Wong, president of the British colony's Legislative Council, is also a member of the provisional legislature picked by a Chinese-appointed panel in December.
The provisional body will replace the Legislative Council when Britain hands the colony back to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
Elizabeth Wong, the legislator who proposed the motion, argued the president should step down from the current council to safeguard the impartiality and integrity of the presidency.
But lawmakers voted 29 to 23 in favour of an amendment put forward by a pro-Beijing member, which changed the motion into an expression of confidence in Wong, local media reported.

Britain has refused to recognise the interim body, saying it has no basis in the 1984 Sino-British handover treaty or in Hong Kong's future mini-constitution, the 1990 Basic Law, that was agreed between London and Beijing.
Local democrats have denounced the provisional body as a sham.
